blocks.content: Pod Security Standards is the modern, built-in way to enforce a baseline security posture across an entire namespace, defining three levels of increasing strictness, enforced simply through namespace labels.

Pod Security Standards defines exactly three levels: Privileged (essentially unrestricted, no meaningful enforcement), Baseline (blocks known, obviously dangerous configurations), and Restricted (the strictest, enforcing current security hardening best practices).

blocks.alt: Three clearly defined levels, from unrestricted to genuinely hardened

blocks.content: Unlike a separate, complex policy object, enforcement is refreshingly simple, a label directly on the namespace itself declares which level applies, Kubernetes enforces it automatically for every Pod created there.

blocks.alt: A simple label doing the enforcement, no separate, complex policy object needed

blocks.content:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: production
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted

code.content:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: production
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted

codes.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: production
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted

blocks.content: The Restricted level requires exactly the kind of security context settings covered in the previous topic, non-root execution, dropped capabilities, no privilege escalation, applied automatically as a baseline requirement for the entire namespace.

blocks.alt: The strictest level, requiring exactly the hardening covered in the Security Context topic

blocks.content: Pod Security Standards is not the original mechanism for this, an older, more complex object called PodSecurityPolicy served a similar role previously, it has since been deprecated and removed, Pod Security Standards is the modern, simpler replacement.

blocks.alt: A simpler, modern replacement for an older, more complex, now-removed mechanism

blocks.content: Pod Security Standards is really the enforcement layer on top of everything covered throughout this module and the Docker Security module, individual Pods can set good securityContext values voluntarily, but a namespace-level Restricted label makes those good practices mandatory, cluster-wide, not just hoped for.

blocks.alt: Turning good individual practices into a mandatory, cluster-enforced baseline

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Pod Security Standards defines three levels (Privileged, Baseline, Restricted), enforced simply through a namespace label, replacing the older, deprecated PodSecurityPolicy.
Restricted enforces exactly the hardening covered in the Security Context and Docker Security modules, turning good individual practices into a mandatory, cluster-wide baseline.
